_meta.author: M. SZUL
_meta.reason: Machine-readable record of what CBMS actually is, traced from live source rather than recalled. Git is the source of truth; the vector database is a derived index that can be rebuilt from this file.

status_vocabulary.CONFIRMED: read from the file or measured from the store on 2026-08-26
status_vocabulary.REFUTED: the claim was checked and is false; the evidence field says how
status_vocabulary.OPEN: not yet checked; do not cite as fact

name.confirmed_by: aions_core/server/codebook_engine.py docstring: 'CBMS Codebook engine: load a small codebook and map EO text <-> CBMS codes.'
name.note: The name describes the intended mechanism - a code book - not the mechanism that carries most of the retrieval traffic today.

findings.claim: CBMS stores knowledge as content-addressed chunks: id = 'K' + first 12 hex of SHA-256(content), uppercased.

evidence.consequence: Identical content overwrites the same file. Deduplication is a property of the address, not of a check.

findings.claim: The intended pipeline is PL/EN -> Esperanto -> codebook symbols -> symbol index.

stages.role: deterministic canonicalisation; a 30-entry dictionary plus regex, explicitly 'not a translator'
greedy longest-phrase-first match, spans marked used so nothing double-matches
symbol -> chunk set, built on the fly, explicitly non-destructive

evidence.why_esperanto: One concept, one form. Polish inflection ('bylem'/'bylam') collapses to a single Esperanto phrase ('mi estis') before any symbol is assigned, so the codebook needs one entry instead of many.

findings.claim: The code book is tiny: 16 symbols.

families.A1-E5: a five-symbol demonstration sentence (byc-past-1sg, dzisiaj, miejsce-sklep, kupic-1sg-past, chleb)
families.CR1-CR5: CRLA tournament vocabulary (system, winner, score, latency, determinism)
families.CB1-CB6: CBMS self-description (system, memory-block, chunk, refusal, panic, facts-keys)

evidence.consequence: A 16-symbol book cannot encode general knowledge. It encodes exactly two things: a demo sentence and the system's own telemetry vocabulary.

findings.claim: Only 13 of 167 live chunks have their content reduced to code-book symbols, and all 13 are CRLA telemetry from one day.

example.pl: CRLA turniej: zwyciezca C04, wynik 0.956, latencja 0.719 ms.
example.eo: crla turniro: gajninto c04, poentaro 0.956, latenco 0.719 ms.

evidence.consequence: The code-book layer works and is proven end to end - on a sentence template it was built for. It was never extended past that template.

findings.claim: Retrieval does not run on the code book. It runs on 'Korean keys' - fixed 3-character blocks.

evidence.mechanism: For each alphanumeric token: character 3-grams of the first 12 chars, prefixed 'g:'; plus two 3-char groups of SHA1(token) hex, prefixed 'h:'. Returns a set. Query and chunk are scored by set overlap.
evidence.korean_content: none - the file contains no Korean character
evidence.what_korean_means_here: an analogy to Hangul, where a syllable packs into one fixed-width block; hence fixed-length 3-character keys
evidence.retrieval_order: aions_core/server/cbms_memory.py cbms_think(): injected context first, then Korean keys (cap 25), then symbolic hits (top 7), then concept buckets (cap 8 each), total capped at 40

findings.claim: Korean characters do appear in CBMS - as chunk addresses, in a different module.

evidence.mechanism: make_hangul_code(data, length=23): SHA1 hex, each hex digit d mapped to chr(ord('가') + d*32)
evidence.measured: 52 of 167 live chunks carry a hangul_code field
evidence.consequence: It is a second name for a chunk, derived from its id. Nothing in retrieval reads it. Purely decorative addressing at present.

findings.claim: 73% of the store was the system's own echo, and the measurement that says so can be reproduced from the filesystem today.

evidence.code_comment: aions_core/server/cbms_memory.py lines 110-130: '73,3% bazy (455 z 621 blokow) to nie wiedza, tylko echo'
evidence.match: The 455 quarantined files are exactly the 455 blocks the comment counted.
evidence.root_cause_recorded_in_code: _should_create_new_chunk() decided to write based on the SHAPE OF THE QUESTION (len>50 or contains 'new'/'how'), not on whether anything had been learned. The system wrote its own echo back as new knowledge.

findings.claim: A write gate now blocks the echo, with eight named rules and a logged rejection trail.

evidence.claimed_accuracy: catches 457 of 621; 455 genuine garbage, 2 empty UNCERTAIN; zero false alarms on the 164 REAL_KNOWLEDGE blocks
evidence.bypass: create_knowledge_chunk(..., bypass_gate=True) for callers that know what they are doing (approved blend ingest, external import)

findings.claim: The reference graph exists, was never read for years, and is still switched off because it is poisoned rather than broken.

evidence.graph_size_recorded_in_code: ~49 000 edges; 90.65% of 49 374 edges lead to the echo blocks
evidence.never_read: audit 2026-08-04: no retrieval code walked 'references'; the graph was written and never read
evidence.why_off: Technically correct (reversible 10/10, zero regression on the first 15 results, ~5 ms overhead) but it surfaces mostly garbage. The synthesis blocks cite each other, forming a self-referential cluster with LOW out-degree, so max_out_degree misses it, and HIGH co-citation, so raising min_support does not help either (min_support=3 tested, cluster survives).
evidence.recorded_order_of_work: first the write gate to stop producing garbage, then cleaning, only then switch the graph on

findings.claim: Claude's thinking patterns and session records are stored inside CBMS blocks.

thinking_patterns.created: 2025-09-09T06:07:06 - a single batch, one second apart
thinking_patterns.shape: CLAUDE THINKING PATTERN: <NAME> / Core Pattern / Methodology (4 numbered steps) / Practical Example / Application Framework

meta_framework.content: HOW TO THINK LIKE CLAUDE - three phases (problem assessment, solution development, ...) each naming which of the six patterns to apply

behaviour_rule.content_first_line: KRYTYCZNA REGULA DLA CLAUDE - OBOWIAZKOWA NA STARCIE KAZDEJ ODPOWIEDZI

findings.claim: Those thinking patterns are stored AS CBMS code.

evidence.what_is_true: They live in CBMS blocks - K + SHA-256 addresses, manifest entries, concept map, reference edges. The container is CBMS.
evidence.what_is_not: Their content is plain English prose. None of the 6 pattern chunks, nor the meta-reasoning chunk, carries an 'eo' or 'cbms_codes' field.
evidence.measured: 13 of 167 chunks carry code-book symbols; all 13 are crla_pattern telemetry (see F04). Zero thinking-pattern chunks are encoded.
evidence.why_it_matters: The distinction decides what work remains: the addressing and storage layer is done for the patterns; the encoding layer was never applied to them. Encoding them would need code-book symbols that do not exist yet - the book has 16.

findings.claim: The 'Korean injection' into Phi-3 encoded CBMS knowledge into model weights.

what_the_numbers_actually_are: 48 mappings = 16 Korean syllables x 3 tensors (q_proj, k_proj, mlp.gate_proj), across layers 0-15 only
each mapping carries a 100-value vector; 4800 values total
those 4800 values measure mean -0.000491, std 0.100013, range -0.369..0.383 - a Gaussian N(0, 0.1), i.e. random noise

the 8 'CBMS blocks' each carry a neural_pattern of 16 vectors x 768 values; all 8 blobs are BYTE-IDENTICAL (sha256 prefix fbfb16c4dc276df7) - the same dictionary was attached to every block rather than one pattern per concept
compression_ratio per block (3.19, 2.85, 4.2, 3.8, 2.95, 3.5, 3.1, 2.9) are hand-written constants, not computed from anything in the file
evidence.independent_confirmation: An earlier weight-level diff of the injected Phi-3 against its base measured the delta as uncorrelated noise: std 0.000995, clipped at +/-2^-8, inter-layer correlation 0.00016. This file is where that noise came from.
evidence.where_the_real_compression_lives: korean_cbms_tokenizer.json, 4016 entries - the 3.19 figure is a tokenizer property, not a weight property. Nothing was learned into the model.

findings.claim: The seed of the whole store is a single script run on 2025-09-09, and its chunks form a hand-built chain, not an organic graph.

evidence.seed_script: direct_memory_inject.py, found in an AIONS_COMPLETE backup under E:\AI_WORKSPACE
evidence.seed_batch: 30 core concepts written at 01:28:39, batch duration ~500 ms
evidence.edge_rule: references = chunk_references[-3:] - each seed chunk points at the previous three. The 'graph' began as a chain with width 3.
evidence.aliases: MAIPA = POLIP = AIONS - the same codebase under names generated by different AI sessions

findings.claim: The manifest disagrees with the filesystem.

evidence.known_history: The counter used to increase unconditionally on every write even though the content hash overwrote the same file; that was fixed on 2026-08-04 by checking chunk_index membership first. The remaining 8 are files present on disk with no manifest entry - direction opposite to the old bug.
evidence.next_step: list the 8 unindexed ids and find which writer created them

findings.claim: There is a CBMS_KR engine family, separate from the modules in this repository.

evidence.claimed_contents: cbms_kr_configs/ holds CBMS_KR (core), cbms_kr_v1, cbms_kr_v1_blend, cbms_kr_v1_broadcast and CBMS_KR_PURE.py; each variant carries an ARCH_CBMS_KR.md manifest
evidence.claimed_use: rebuild Korean Keys, or repair a corrupted kb.mmap
evidence.claimed_integration: a thinking pattern names the CBMS_KR variant it needs - ITERATIVE_REFINEMENT is said to require cbms_kr_v1_blend
evidence.status_note: None of this has been opened and verified. The chunk is a claim by an earlier session, not a measurement. Treat as a lead.

chunk_record.reading: The optional fields are strata. Each group of 8 or 16 is one writer that ran once and left its own shape behind.

open_questions: Which 8 chunk files have no manifest entry, and which writer created them? (F14)
Open the CBMS_KR variants and check whether they are a real engine family or another self-report. (F15)

The code book has 16 symbols and encodes one demo sentence plus telemetry. Is growing it the right move, or is the Korean-key layer the one that should carry retrieval permanently? Nothing measured yet compares the two on the same queries.
chunks_quarantine holds 455 blocks. Is any of it recoverable, or is quarantine effectively deletion with a longer name?
